Fixed the normal HTTP acquisition path's (scripts/source-acquisition/src/acquire.mjs) lock-overwrite/no-PDF-validation defect that the case-003 MIC survey surfaced: lock() previously wrote the canonical raw file unconditionally and unconditionally replaced any existing lock entry, with no content-type validation (a WAF/challenge page returning 2xx could have been locked as if it were the real PDF, exactly the METI risk class). Extracted the immutable lock-decision/mutation policy (decideLockAction/applyAcquisition, previously only in browser-fetch.mjs) into a new shared module, scripts/source-acquisition/src/lock-policy.mjs, used by both acquire.mjs and browser-fetch.mjs -- so the invariant (identical re-fetch is a no-op; mismatched re-fetch fails loudly with both SHA-256 values, never mutating the lock or raw file; PDF-magic-byte validation before any write) is acquisition-method-independent, not just Playwright-specific. Covered by 8 new tests (scripts/source-acquisition/src/test.mjs, fixture/injected-download based, no live network); all 7 existing browser-fetch tests still pass unchanged. All 4 existing locked sources (case-001 x2, METI case-002, MIC case-003 candidate) verified byte-identical, in both sources/source-lock.json and sources/raw/, before and after the fix.
